subject.title: Feature: Agent 动态切换命令（不重启 Gateway）

question: Should OpenClaw support a channel-level `/agent <id>` temporary configured-agent switch, and if so which authorization and state-ownership contract should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting this feature changes who owns an active chat's workspace, credentials, tools, memory, transcript, and session route, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Authorize conversation-level switch
options.body: Implement `/agent <id>` as an explicit, opt-in conversation binding to configured agents with sender authorization, per-agent session isolation, TTL/reset semantics, and cross-channel tests.

options.title: Limit to existing session binding
options.body: Keep configured-agent switching out of core chat commands and document `/focus`, ACP bindings, static `bindings`, or channel/account separation as the supported paths.

options.title: Decline core command for now
options.body: Close or defer the request until a broader multi-agent command-targeting contract covers `/agent`, `/new`, `/reset`, and related cross-agent controls together.

recommendation.title: Authorize conversation-level switch
recommendation.body: Implement `/agent <id>` as an explicit, opt-in conversation binding to configured agents with sender authorization, per-agent session isolation, TTL/reset semantics, and cross-channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across routing, command registry, and current conversation binding surfaces affected by the decision.
